replication.target_description: Swedish nationwide nested case–control antipsychotic exposure/breast cancer study; row-specific exposure duration, drug group and model unresolved.

notes:
Identity assessment: this is a substantive primary-report web-text parse, containing Methods, Results, Tables 1–5, Discussion, author contributions and affiliations. The contributor list matches all eight supplied replication authors, including Marco Solmi, Olivier Corbeil, Ellenor Mittendorfer-Rutz and Heidi Taipale. The described Swedish nationwide nested case–control replication of the Finnish breast-cancer study matches the supplied project and design. However, the parse begins at Introduction and supplies no article title/header, DOI sbae058, journal issue, year or pagination; exact bibliographic identity cannot be independently fully confirmed from this candidate alone. It is not an abstract-only excerpt or a preregistration. No PDF is supplied, so page 5 cannot be verified and section/table locators are used.
All four assigned rows have identical neutral descriptions, study identifiers and p. 5 locators. They do not identify exposure duration, drug group, adjustment, subgroup or sensitivity analysis. Table 2 has adjusted OR candidates: prolactin-increasing 1–<5 years 1.20 (95% CI 1.03–1.41), ≥5 years 1.47 (1.26–1.71); prolactin-sparing 1–<5 years 1.17 (0.98–1.40), ≥5 years 0.99 (0.78–1.26), each against <1 year. Unadjusted alternatives are also printed; Tables 3–5 contain further dose, sensitivity and subgroup candidates. No candidate is assigned to an audit row by order, count or numerical matching. The increasing-versus-sparing wording does not establish a direct between-drug-group contrast: the main analyses compare duration categories within each drug class, mutually adjusted.
Common main-model sample candidate only: 1642 case entries + 8173 matched-control entries = 9815 case/control entries, from the final included groups, not the 132061-woman source cohort. Controls could subsequently become cases, so this is not established as 9815 distinct women. Main duration analyses use the common Table 2 groups; Table 5 subgroup samples differ. Exclusions: previous cancer other than nonmelanoma skin cancer, HIV, mastectomy or organ transplant; controls have the same exclusion criteria, cases aged 18–85 with ≥4.5 years medication history. Because the row-specific model is unresolved, this common N is retained only as a candidate for parent field-scope review, with no positive core n.
Inspected Statistical Analyses, Results and Tables 2–5: ORs and 95% confidence intervals are provided, with no numerical same-test p value or p bound in these displayed analyses. No p is derived from confidence intervals or narrative significance. This absence is limited to the supplied parse; missing article front matter and unavailable PDF prevent claims about unobserved material.
